title: Fit the child container to the branch shape
description: Choose a key workload and a node representation. The model compares approximate memory, expected path depth, and transition behavior without pretending one layout wins everywhere.

workloads.label: Lowercase autocomplete
workloads.detail: Many words share early prefixes, while most deeper nodes have only one or two children.

workloads.label: Multilingual catalog
workloads.detail: A large key-unit space makes preallocated child slots especially expensive.

workloads.label: Static routing prefixes
workloads.detail: Builds are infrequent and long single-child paths make compression attractive.

workloads.label: Dense command alphabet
workloads.detail: Shallow nodes use much of a small alphabet and favor predictable direct transitions.

representations.label: Fixed child array
representations.detail: One pointer slot per alphabet unit gives direct indexing but pays for empty slots.

representations.label: Hash-map children
representations.detail: Allocate entries only for present transitions at the cost of hashing and map metadata.

representations.label: Sorted compact edges
representations.detail: Pack present edges contiguously and binary-search them for better locality.

representations.label: Compressed radix nodes
representations.detail: Collapse single-child paths into segments; static sparse keys benefit most.
